name: read-guard-prose-defect
body:
source: navigator/user brief — the four distributed agents' `## File access (strict)` prose contradicts their own permission frontmatter.

evidence (read on this branch; `.md` files are not scanned code, so these are file facts, not graph facts): `opencode-suite/agents/spec-review.md:70-74`, `spec-writer.md:98-104`, `plan-writer.md:85-89`, `plan-review.md:109-113` each say, verbatim, "You may read any file and query the code graph, but you **never modify any file** …". The same files' frontmatter denies `read`/`glob`/`grep` on `apg/.trans/**`, `apg/layers/**`, and the worktree mirrors `apg/.worktrees/*/apg/.trans/**` / `apg/.worktrees/*/apg/layers/**` (spec-review.md:7-26, mirrored in the other three). The prose thus claims exactly the access the guard denies. The correct instruction exists but is weaker/buried — spec-review.md:100 ("Read node bodies via the graph; read source files behind code FQNs with the `read` tool") and the essential-rules item 6 only make raw reads a non-fallback on tool failure; neither overrides the blanket claim. `codebase-navigator.md:113-117` already states the correct rule ("the durable spec and the transient plan/review state are reached through those tools too, never by reading raw files"), and `agent-builder.md:73-91` requires the deny for generated agents but not the positive prose. Observed consequence: a spec-review run (session-ses_f64e) retried `read apg/layers/.../coordinator-mediated-feedback.json` and was denied every time, burning the run instead of reading the spec through `apg_query`/`apg_review`.

inconsistency: the prose claims read-anything while the grant denies the graph-state paths — a violation of `domain.value.prose-grant-alignment`, not covered by `domain.constraint.no-internals-in-prose` (which forbids naming the paths, not claiming the access).

resolution [with user / navigator brief]: rewrite the four `## File access (strict)` sections to state the rule plainly (graph state reached only through the apg tools; never read those node/transient files directly; ordinary source files behind code FQNs stay readable with `read`), and extend `agent-builder.md`'s permission-shape list + step-6 checklist so generated agents inherit the positive rule. Authored as `requirements.requirement.read-guard-prose` (+3 children), `domain.value.prose-grant-alignment`, `domain.constraint.prose-matches-grant`, and `solution.component.file-access-guard-prose`. Scope is only the agent prompt files (product source embedded via `include_str!`); nothing in the Rust control flow changes, so the solution anchors to the embedding/install Rust (`apg.main`, `apg.install_suite`), never to a `.md` path. [with user]
